text: {"main_idea":"The source asks for a literature review on multimedia resources in mobile-assisted language learning. It also gives a rubric with many required sections, citations, theories, studies, and format rules.","key_points":["The review must have Introduction, Main Body, Conclusion, and References sections.","It must focus only on multimedia resources used in MALL and not on unrelated topics.","It should use authentic scholarly sources that can be found on Google Scholar.","It must discuss theory, empirical studies, design factors, ethics, and future research, including AI or adaptive personalization."]}

{"main_idea":"The text asks for a research-paper introduction on cloud cybersecurity in multi-tenant cloud environments. It says the introduction should explain current defenses, their limits, and then present a new security framework.","key_points":["It stresses the growth of cloud computing and the importance of multi-tenant architectures for modern enterprise IT.","It says shared resources in multi-tenant clouds increase the attack surface and can lead to cross-tenant data breaches and other attacks.","It asks for an analysis of encryption, isolation, and access management, including their practical weaknesses in real systems.","It requires a smooth transition from these limits to a novel, practical framework that unifies and improves cloud security."]}

{"main_idea":"This text asks for a scholarly section on the theoretical and practical significance of a blockchain trust mechanism for collaborative product design in cloud manufacturing. It requires a clear academic structure and emphasizes both new theory and real industrial value.","key_points":["The section must have an opening paragraph, then separate Theoretical Significance and Practical Significance headings.","The theoretical part should explain decentralized trust, objective trust evaluation, blockchain architecture, smart contracts, and security or governance ideas.","The practical part should cover IP protection, non-repudiation, audit trails, workflow automation, compliance, scalability, and new business uses.","The response must use formal engineering-journal language and link each theory claim to a practical benefit without overstatement."]}

{"main_idea":"The text gives a detailed assignment brief for a methodology section in a research paper. It asks for a VR healthcare training system with physical device integration and real-time data synchronization.","key_points":["The section must focus only on VR simulation design, device integration, and synchronization, not results or unrelated background.","The writing style must be formal, academic, and suitable for a medical technology journal.","The methodology should be organized into clear subsections and describe the full system architecture and VR platform.","The brief emphasizes novel features such as live device links, semantic middleware, bi-directional control, and technical validation with latency and synchronization measures."]}

{"main_idea":"The source text gives an assignment brief for a long critical essay on the child narrator in *The Catcher in the Rye*. It also gives strict scoring rules for thesis, quotations, criticism, structure, style, and a works cited page.","key_points":["The essay must focus on one central argument about Holden Caulfield as a child narrator.","It must use direct novel quotations and exact critic quotations with clear attribution.","It must analyze unreliability, innocence, trauma, and post-war American context.","It must end with a Conclusion heading and a properly formatted Works Cited page."]}

{"main_idea":"The source text gives an assignment brief for a long critical essay on the opening of *The Catcher in the Rye*. It asks for a single central argument about Holden Caulfield as a different child narrator, supported by critics, theorists, and close textual analysis.","key_points":["The essay must focus only on the opening chapter or paragraphs of the novel.","It must argue one clear, debatable idea about Holden's narrative difference.","It must use quotations from Salinger and cite theorists and critics in academic style.","It must be organized, detailed, and written in an authoritative critical voice with limited plot summary."]}

{"main_idea":"The source gives a writing assignment about the philosophy of Japanese gardens. It asks for a long essay shaped by Bashō’s travel writing and garden ideas, with specific structure and content requirements.","key_points":["The essay must be about 1,600 to 2,300 words and have an introduction, body sections, and a conclusion.","It should use Bashō’s haiku and The Narrow Road to the Deep North as a lens for garden philosophy.","It must include the exact Bashō excerpt and connect it to Japanese garden ideas like impermanence, journey, and design.","It also requires named garden masters, Japanese terms, maintenance as meditation, and many specific design and style elements."]}

{"main_idea":"The text gives an assignment to write a critical essay on Haushofer's Pan-Ideas and demography. It also gives a long rubric that sets strict rules for format, citations, content, and length.","key_points":["The essay must be a formal critical essay with a clear title, introduction, body headings, and conclusion.","It must focus on Haushofer, Pan-regions, demography, state power, and imperial expansion.","It must use in-text citations with page numbers and include a matching reference list.","It must meet detailed content rules about historical context, ethics, scholarship, and word count."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how Python variables and scope work. It also covers global, nonlocal, and how to inspect names with locals and globals.","key_points":["Variables are created by assignment and are references to objects, not typed values.","Names exist only in the current or global scope, and scope is set by function and class blocks.","Global names can be read in functions, but plain assignment needs a global declaration to modify them.","Nonlocal lets a nested function change a variable in an outer function, and locals and globals return scope dictionaries."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how Python 2 uses exceptions to report and handle errors. It also says exceptions can be custom, cleaned up with a final clause, and sometimes used for control flow.","key_points":["Python raises built-in exceptions for errors and unusual conditions like file limits or divide by zero.","You can catch exceptions with handling blocks, but catching every exception is usually a bad idea.","Exceptions can move up the call stack until a matching handler is found.","The text also mentions custom exceptions, cleanup with a final clause, and using exceptions to leave code early."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how C strings work and how the string library is organized. It says strings use a null terminator, and strcat can join strings only when there is enough space.","key_points":["C string literals use double quotes and end with a zero-valued null character.","Backslash escapes are used for special or control characters in string literals.","Wide strings use wchar_t, have their own functions, and may need more than one wchar_t per character.","The string library has different kinds of functions, and strcat can cause overflow if the first string is not large enough."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains basic Python control flow. It focuses on loops and branches, and says function calls are covered later.","key_points":["Python has two main loop types: for loops and while loops.","For loops go through items in a sequence, and range helps create number sequences.","While loops repeat until a condition is false, and they can use else, break, and continue.","Python uses if, elif, and else for branches, and indentation shows what code belongs to each block."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains what computer programming is and how it fits into software engineering. It also says that learning to be a good programmer matters more than choosing one specific language.","key_points":["Programming is writing source code that a computer can interpret or compile to do useful work.","Programming is part of software engineering, while computer science is more theoretical.","Markup languages are usually not considered programming, though some can include scripts or act as programming languages.","Good programmers learn concepts, algorithms, and sometimes more than one language, and different language families can feel very different."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains basic UNIX network programming in C. It covers simple client and server setup, common socket functions, and a few related networking tools.","key_points":["A client uses a socket and an address struct to connect to a remote server and receive data.","Data must be null terminated after receiving, and sending may need retries if not all bytes are sent.","A server binds a socket to a port, listens for connections, and accepts a session socket for each client.","The text also notes useful host lookup functions, UDP alternatives, and that many network calls return -1 on failure."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains aspect oriented programming as a follow-on to object oriented programming. It says AOP helps handle cross-cutting concerns like logging and persistence without repeating code in many classes.","key_points":["OOP organizes software into objects, but large programs still have concerns that do not fit well inside single objects.","Cross-cutting concerns appear in many unrelated parts of a program and can break encapsulation and add dependencies.","AOP moves code for those concerns into separate aspects and weaves them back into the source automatically.","Logging and persistence are given as common examples of cross-cutting concerns that AOP can centralize."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains basic file I/O in Python 2.6. It also shows how to save and load phone numbers with files.","key_points":["A file object is created first, then it can be read from or written to, and finally it should be closed.","Writing uses a command that adds each phone entry as one line with a name, comma, number, and newline.","Reading uses a loop with a command until an empty string shows the end of the file.","The example phone program now has load and save options, and the exercise asks to add file I/O to the grades program."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains how to start writing and running Python programs. It uses a simple Hello, World example to show the basic file and terminal steps.","key_points":["Python programs are plain text files that you can edit with any text editor.","A text editor with Python syntax highlighting can make writing code easier.","The Hello, World program prints a message and then ends.","The text gives different terminal commands and steps for Windows, Mac, and Linux to run the program."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how the thalamus relays sensory information and how the cerebral cortex maps the body. It also shows that body maps keep the same topographic order from the spinal pathways through the thalamus to the cortex, with sensitive areas taking more space.","key_points":["The thalamus is a major relay between the cerebrum and the rest of the nervous system.","Most sensory signals must pass through the thalamus before reaching the cerebral cortex, but smell is the main exception.","The thalamus has anterior, medial, and lateral nuclei with different links to the hypothalamus, limbic system, basal ganglia, and sensory cortex.","The somatosensory cortex contains a homunculus that keeps body positions in order and gives more space to sensitive areas like the fingers and lower face."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how to choose business location, equipment, and vehicles. It says cost, taxes, and long-term value must be checked before buying or leasing.","key_points":["Budget limits should guide which locations you can afford.","Location choices should weigh visibility, foot traffic, upkeep, taxes, insurance, and renovation costs.","Businesses should value used equipment for tax purposes and confirm its useful life.","Vehicle buyers should compare purchase and lease tax benefits and use reliable price guides."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains journal entries and interest costs for bonds from the issuer’s view. It also compares bond accounting rules under IFRS and US GAAP, with a key difference in interest amortization.","key_points":["Bond cash flows include cash received at issue and repayment at maturity.","The journal entries are made from the issuer’s side, so the investor records the opposite entries.","Bond interest payments stay the same by the bond terms, but recognized interest cost can change over time under effective interest.","US GAAP may allow straight-line amortization if it is not materially different, but IFRS allows only the effective-interest method."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how managers use communication and writing to make decisions and create meaning. It also warns that information is interpreted by people, not facts alone.","key_points":["Managers use informal talk to gather information and share views before formal channels.","Writing is a major part of organizational life and helps with analysis, proof, and decisions.","Managers should write clearly and never send a first draft or sign work they would not defend.","Communication shapes what things mean, and people may interpret the same facts in different ways."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how households can save and invest their funds. It says these choices should be judged by expected return, risk, and liquidity.","key_points":["Households can place savings in bank deposits, bonds, stocks, mutual funds, money market funds, or tangible assets like housing and gold.","Expected rate of return is the average gain an investment is expected to pay over time.","Risk is the uncertainty that actual returns will differ from what was expected.","High-risk investments can have returns that are much above or much below the expected return."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how divergence measures outward flow from a point. It also uses the divergence theorem to justify a case of Gauss’ law for a point charge.","key_points":["Divergence is interpreted as net outward flux per unit volume near a point.","A small ball around the point lets the divergence theorem connect flux and divergence.","The divergence theorem helps write physical laws in both integral and differential forms.","For a point charge at the origin, the text aims to show the flux is zero outside the surface and q/ε0 inside it."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how oxygen and ozone changed Earth and helped life spread on land. It also says that finding a second example of life would show that life may be common in the universe.","key_points":["Ozone made by sunlight and oxygen helped block harmful ultraviolet radiation.","This protection let life move from the oceans onto land.","More oxygen killed some microbes but gave others a rich new energy source.","A second example of life in our solar system or nearby would suggest life is common, so we must choose where to search."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how bias and conflict can make decision-making harder. It says good managers should look at issues from more than one view and avoid personal attacks.","key_points":["People resist challenges to their beliefs and often ignore evidence that does not fit what they already think.","We tend to favor people we like and distrust people we dislike, which can distort our judgments.","Conflict can be necessary for good long-term decisions even when it feels uncomfortable in the short term.","Process conflict can help solve problems, but relationship conflict is harmful and should be reduced."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how seismic waves and sound waves move and what affects their speeds. It also shows that P-waves are faster than S-waves, and that sound speed in gases depends on temperature only weakly.","key_points":["Earthquakes have P-waves and S-waves that travel at different speeds.","In granite, P-waves are much faster because the bulk modulus is greater than the shear modulus.","Both wave types move slower in less rigid material, and the P-S time gap helps find the epicenter.","Sound speed in air and gases depends on temperature, but only through a square-root relation."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains lean business practices and continuous improvement methods. It says these methods can improve performance, but they also need careful cost control and can be hard to implement.","key_points":["Lean business models try to remove waste while still meeting the company mission.","Managerial accounting helps lean work by giving accurate cost and performance information.","Continuous improvement includes practices like total quality management, just-in-time manufacturing, and Lean Six Sigma.","Just-in-time manufacturing lowers inventory costs but is complex and can be disrupted by supply chain problems."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains visceral sensation, referred pain, and visceral reflex pathways. It shows that internal pain can be felt in distant body areas because nerve pathways meet at similar spinal levels.","key_points":["Baroreceptors from the carotid arteries travel in the glossopharyngeal nerve, and those from the aorta travel in the vagus nerve.","Strong visceral sensations can reach awareness, but they are often felt in unexpected places called referred pain.","A common theory says referred pain happens because visceral and somatosensory fibers enter the spinal cord at the same level.","The text also describes efferent visceral reflexes, which use preganglionic and ganglionic neurons in sympathetic and parasympathetic pathways."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains several plant hormones and how plants respond to touch and wind. It shows that these signals control dormancy, ripening, defense, growth, and rapid movements.","key_points":["ABA helps seeds stay dormant through cold seasons and supports winter bud development.","Ethylene promotes fruit ripening, leaf fall, flower wilting, and some germination.","Jasmonates, oligosaccharins, strigolactones, and brassinosteroids affect defense and development.","Plants also show thigmotropism, such as tendril coiling, Venus flytrap closure, and mimosa leaf folding."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how accountants work in public firms, corporations, and government. It shows that each setting has different tasks, rules, and certifications, but all focus on accurate financial information and control.","key_points":["Public accounting firms often want CPAs and may specialize by industry or by services like tax planning.","Corporate accountants provide information for managers and help with costs, budgets, payroll, controls, and audits.","Large corporations may use Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, CMA certification, and sometimes CPAs.","Government accountants track taxpayer funds under GASB rules and may work on tax compliance or fraud investigations."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains utilitarian ethics and links it to business and accounting decisions. It says good decisions should consider all stakeholders and both short-term and long-term effects.","key_points":["Utilitarianism says the best action gives the greatest good for the greatest number of people.","A utilitarian business decision tries to maximize utility for all stakeholders, not only shareholders.","Financial statements help business owners make short-term and long-term decisions from cash and other financial information.","The Chris example shows cash basis accounting and how owners use it to understand income, expenses, and future planning."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how monopolistic competition moves toward long-run equilibrium. It also compares its efficiency with perfect competition and shows that long-run economic profit is zero, not accounting profit.","key_points":["Positive economic profits attract new firms and push the original firm’s demand and marginal revenue left.","Economic losses cause firms to exit, which raises demand for the remaining firms and reduces losses.","In the long run, entry and exit drive monopolistically competitive firms to zero economic profit.","This market is not productively or allocatively efficient, so it usually has higher prices and lower output than perfect competition."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how to find the center of mass of a thin lamina with constant density. It shows that this center of mass depends on the shape of the region and leads to formulas using mass and moments.","key_points":["A lamina is treated as a thin two-dimensional sheet with constant density.","For constant density, the center of mass depends only on the region's shape and is its centroid.","To find the center of mass, we need the total mass and the moments about the x- and y-axes.","The text begins a rectangle-based approximation by using small rectangles with mass ρf(xi*)Δx."]}

{"main_idea":"The text describes several eukaryotic cell organelles and how plant and animal cells differ. It also explains that these organelles have specialized jobs in storage, digestion, protection, and energy use.","key_points":["Peroxisomes break down fatty acids and amino acids and help detoxify poisons.","Vesicles and vacuoles are membrane sacs used in storage and transport, but their membranes behave differently.","Animal cells have centrosomes and lysosomes, while most plant cells do not.","Plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts, and a large central vacuole, and chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains the law of conservation of charge. It says total charge never changes, even when charge moves, particles are created, or particles annihilate.","key_points":["Charge is not created or destroyed, and total charge stays constant in any process.","A closed system keeps the same charge unless charge is transferred in or out.","In open systems, the charge change equals the charge transferred across the boundary.","When charged particles are created or annihilated, equal and opposite charges appear or disappear so the total charge remains zero."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains several key decisional roles of managers. It shows that managers must make choices, handle change, manage crises, allocate scarce resources, and negotiate with others.","key_points":["Managers decide for the organization and its stakeholders even when information is unclear.","As entrepreneurs, managers try to improve the business and adapt to change.","As crisis handlers, managers must respond to problems that are often unexpected.","Managers also allocate limited resources and spend much time negotiating."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains the citric acid cycle in cellular respiration. It shows how acetyl CoA is broken down in mitochondria to release CO2 and make energy carriers.","key_points":["The cycle has several names, including the citric acid cycle, the TCA cycle, and the Krebs cycle.","It happens in the mitochondrial matrix and is a closed loop that regenerates oxaloacetate.","The cycle is aerobic because its NADH and FADH2 must pass electrons to later steps that use oxygen.","Each acetyl group yields two CO2, three NADH, one FADH2, and one ATP or GTP."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains direct cell signaling through gap junctions and plasmodesmata, and it also describes internal receptors. These systems let cells share signals or respond to ligands that can enter the cell, which helps control gene expression and development.","key_points":["Gap junctions in animals and plasmodesmata in plants connect neighboring cells for direct signaling.","Small signaling molecules can pass through these channels, but large molecules cannot.","This signaling can help neighboring cells coordinate their response and support proper embryological development.","Internal receptors are inside the cell and bind hydrophobic ligands that cross the plasma membrane."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains major immune system disorders, especially inherited immunodeficiencies and HIV/AIDS. It also introduces hypersensitivity as an immune reaction that is stronger than normal.","key_points":["SCID is a severe inherited immunodeficiency that affects both B cells and T cells and is usually fatal without treatment.","Bone marrow transplants can rebuild the immune system, and gene therapy may help when standard transplants do not.","HIV spreads through semen, vaginal fluids, blood, and needle sharing, and it gradually destroys CD4+ helper T cells.","HIV drugs can prolong life, but a vaccine remains difficult because the virus changes rapidly; hypersensitivity means an abnormally strong immune response."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains what marketing research is and how companies use it. It shows that research helps firms understand customers and make better marketing decisions.","key_points":["Marketing research plans, collects, and analyzes data for marketing decisions.","It gives information about customer preferences, product benefits, and lifestyles.","Companies use primary data and secondary data in marketing research.","Primary data can come from surveys, observation, or experiments to study customer behavior and sales."]}

{"main_idea":"This study examines how temperature, pH, and water activity affect Penicillium expansum growth and patulin production. It also builds a model to predict the fungus growth rate and help control storage and processing risks.","key_points":["Penicillium expansum is a widespread fungus that can spoil fruit and produce the toxic compound patulin.","The study aims to separate conditions that favor fungal growth from conditions that favor patulin production.","A mathematical model was developed to estimate growth rate from temperature, pH, and water activity.","The model predicted the best growth at 24°C, pH 5.1, and water activity 0.99, and it worked on contaminated apples."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains Zoology research and teaching in Brazil and introduces the Summer Course in Zoology, or CVZoo. It says the course was created to spread knowledge and give graduate students teaching practice, in a field with strong regional inequality.","key_points":["Brazil has great animal diversity, but Zoology knowledge is still incomplete.","Researchers, publications, graduate programs, and funding are mostly concentrated in the South and Southeast.","The unequal pattern makes wider actions urgent to spread teaching and research across the country.","CVZoo began in January 2013 at the University of São Paulo to share Zoology research and train graduate students as teachers."]}

{"main_idea":"This text reports a study on cataract surgery rate at MAIWP-Hospital Selayang in Malaysia. It shows that better access through a smart partnership helped increase surgery and support blindness prevention.","key_points":["Cataract is a major cause of blindness, especially in low- and middle-income countries.","The study estimated cataract surgery rate and described patients treated from 2013 to 2016.","The surgery rate changed over time, rising in 2014, falling in 2015, and rising again in 2016.","Female patients were more than male patients, and the average surgery time was about 21 minutes."]}

{"main_idea":"This text reports a study of herpes zoster trends in Japan using national medical claims data. It finds no significant change in the first half of the year after routine varicella immunization began.","key_points":["Herpes zoster is common in older people and can cause painful rash and long lasting neuralgia.","Japan lacked national surveillance for herpes zoster, so the study used the NDBEMC claims database.","The analysis focused on people aged 65 years or older and adjusted for data coverage.","The routine varicella immunization started in October 2014, but its estimated effect was not significant with the time trend model."]}

{"main_idea":"This text introduces the importance of choosing the right location for service facilities, especially vehicle maintenance stations. It says that site selection is a key problem because it affects cost, service, and customer satisfaction.","key_points":["A good location can reduce cost and improve customer satisfaction.","Heavy-duty vehicle repair stations are important for vehicle travel and after-sales service.","Many scholars have studied site selection with mathematical models and heuristic algorithms.","Related work includes stochastic, multi-level, and multi-objective planning models for different facility types."]}

{"main_idea":"The text describes a study of ataxin-2-like protein and its possible role in RNA metabolism. It shows that ATXN2L helps regulate stress granules and processing bodies.","key_points":["ATXN2L is a paralog of ataxin-2 and shares several conserved motifs with it.","The protein is widely expressed and may overlap in function with ATXN2.","The study found that ATXN2L interacts with DDX6, PABP, and ATXN2.","ATXN2L is a component of stress granules and affects stress granules and P-bodies when its levels change."]}

{"main_idea":"The text describes a study of brain tissue from fetal and infant deaths. It examines BDNF in the Kölliker-Fuse nucleus to compare unexplained deaths with control cases.","key_points":["The study included 45 brains from stillbirths and infants who died between 1 hour and 6 months of age.","Italian law required thorough post-mortem investigation for sudden infant death and unexplained fetal death cases.","The brainstem was sampled and stained with routine methods and immunohistochemistry for BDNF, apoptosis, and GFAP.","Twenty-nine cases remained unexplained and were labeled SIUDS or SIDS, while 16 cases had a known cause of death and served as controls."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains a low-complexity FPGA design for an LDPC decoder. It says the new decoder uses normalized Min-sum and is smaller in hardware use than older serial and partial parallel designs.","key_points":["LDPC codes are used in satellite and wireless systems because they decode well and are easy to implement.","Serial decoders are simple but slow, while full parallel decoders are fast but too complex for hardware.","The proposed decoder uses the normalized Min-sum algorithm and a dual-port Block RAM on FPGA.","The design uses two-channel parallel decoding and 6-bit quantization to reduce resource use while keeping performance acceptable."]}

{"main_idea":"This review looks at what affects the retention of aged care workers. It finds that both personal and workplace factors help keep staff, while understaffing and poor conditions push them away.","key_points":["The review included 49 studies on care workers in aged care settings and home care.","It found two main groups of retention factors: individual factors and organisational factors.","Personal satisfaction, good relationships, and a cooperative culture support retention.","Training, career growth, fair pay, job stability, and injury prevention also support retention, while heavy workloads and stress increase turnover."]}

{"main_idea":"This text studies how miR-874 affects angiogenesis in gastric cancer. It shows that miR-874 is low in cancer and can suppress angiogenesis by blocking STAT3 and VEGF-A.","key_points":["miR-874 was lower in gastric cancer tissues and cell lines than in normal gastric cells.","The study links miR-874 to reduced tumor growth, migration, invasion, and microvessel density.","miR-874 targets the 3'-UTR of STAT3 mRNA and inhibits the STAT3 pathway.","This leads to lower VEGF-A, so miR-874 may be a therapeutic target in gastric cancer."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains genetic connectedness in breeding evaluation. It says connectedness helps compare animals across groups and is important when groups are not well linked.","key_points":["Genetic evaluation aims to predict merit with high accuracy and low bias.","Comparing animals across groups is hard when genetic connectedness is weak.","This problem matters in New Zealand sheep breeding with many flocks and groups.","Earlier work defined connectedness through predictability, information loss, and the CD statistic."]}

{"main_idea":"This text studies battery sizing for mild P2 hybrid electric vehicles with thermal limits. It shows that small passive batteries can overheat, while a larger battery can lower fuel use without thermal problems.","key_points":["Small passively cooled battery packs are common in mild hybrid electric vehicles.","Continuous electric traction can cause thermal runaway, shorter life, and fire risk.","The paper uses an electro-thermal model and a supervisory controller with thermal limits.","A 0.9 kWh pack raised fuel use by 2–3% and reached 180 C, while a 1.8 kWh pack cut fuel use by 8–13% without thermal issues."]}

{"main_idea":"This text describes a plasmonic nanoswitch experiment studied by fluorescence microscopy. It shows that silver nanoparticle monolayers can boost the fluorescence signals from the molecule layer near them.","key_points":["The sample used a PMMA film doped with 1a on a triangular AgNP monolayer on glass.","The AgNPs were about 90 ± 9 nm and were made to create strong local plasmon fields.","The film thickness and nanoparticle coverage placed many molecules close to the enhanced field region.","With 633 nm excitation, the AgNP sample gave stronger fluorescence and more detected events than the control, while background scattering stayed steady without burst-like signals."]}

{"main_idea":"The text studies nitrous oxide emissions in African ecosystems. It shows that emissions are higher in Kenyan agricultural fields than in a Senegal savanna grassland, and that soil water and nitrate are key drivers.","key_points":["The study combines field measurements from Senegal and Kenya with a 1D model for a semi-arid site in Dahra.","N 2 O emissions were larger in the Mbita agricultural fields than at the Dahra grassland site.","Soil water and nitrate were the main factors linked to seasonal N 2 O emissions in both regions.","The model captured the seasonal pattern well, but the usual water-filled pore space trigger should be reconsidered for semi-arid ecosystems."]}

{"main_idea":"The text introduces a study on what affects children's physical activity. It says the study uses UK cohort data and accelerometers to test home and neighbourhood influences.","key_points":["Physical activity is linked to better health and well-being.","Activity rates are low among UK children, especially girls.","Past studies gave mixed results and often had design limits.","This study uses a large UK cohort and measures both objective and subjective environments."]}

{"main_idea":"This text describes methods used to study KCNQ4 channel mutants in HEK293T cells. The work examines how the mutants affect channel surface expression and conductance, which is linked to sensorineural hearing loss.","key_points":["WT and mutant KCNQ4 constructs were made with Myc or HA tags and verified by DNA sequencing.","HEK293T cells were transfected with these constructs for imaging and electrophysiology studies.","Immunofluorescence, co-immunoprecipitation, and surface protein isolation were used to study channel location and interactions.","Western blotting was used to detect proteins and compare band signals after normalization to GAPDH."]}

{"main_idea":"The text is a case study about primary curriculum change in Lesotho and the role of foreign curriculum experts. It shows that curriculum reform is costly and often needs outside help, but local context and teacher readiness matter a lot.","key_points":["Curriculum change is frequent, but it is expensive and needs materials, training, and expert support.","South Africa's C2005 showed how foreign ideas can shape reform, but local conditions may make implementation difficult.","Lesotho has repeatedly used foreign curriculum experts because local curriculum expertise is limited.","The study uses qualitative semi-structured interviews with curriculum specialists, directors, and consultants in Lesotho."]}

{"main_idea":"The text presents a new method for clustering similar alarm floods in industrial control systems. It says the method uses alarm sequences and coactivations, and it gives better and more meaningful clusters than older approaches.","key_points":["Industrial plants produce large alarm and sensor data that can help data mining and machine learning.","Alarm floods are hard to handle because many alarms happen together and may share a root cause.","The paper proposes a novel clustering approach that uses dynamic alarm behavior and coactivations.","The new method improves accuracy and reduces high dimensionality and computational complexity."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains the study methods used to examine mobile phone use by small-scale farmers in Zimbabwe. It also describes the statistical model used to see what factors affect adoption of mobile ICTs in agriculture.","key_points":["Researchers interviewed and surveyed farmers in Svosve-Wenimbi, Marondera district, from July to September 2015.","The sample used stratified random sampling across four wards and included 131 farmers, both men and women.","The data were analysed with SPSS, and descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were used to study ownership and agribusiness use.","A binomial logit model tested whether households adopted mobile ICTs based on factors such as gender, age, education, farm income, crops, and extension source."]}

{"main_idea":"The text reports an analytical evaluation of a BNP test on the new respons®IQ point-of-care platform. It shows that the test meets basic performance, stability, and comparison requirements for POC use.","key_points":["respons®IQ is a microfluidic POC system with TIRF detection and optical sensor control.","A BNP assay was developed to test heart failure and acute coronary syndrome use.","The study measured sensitivity, imprecision, cartridge storage stability, and correlation to reference systems.","The BNP test showed low detection limits, good precision, long refrigerated stability, and high correlation with reference methods."]}

{"main_idea":"The text reports a DNS study of stably stratified open channel flow. It finds that weak large-scale vortices appear at the edges of laminar and turbulent patches and may help keep the intermittent flow stable.","key_points":["The paper studies vorticity balance in a stably stratified open channel flow.","The simulation used a moving reference frame so laminar and turbulent patches stayed nearly fixed.","Time averaging then revealed weak large-scale vortex structures near patch boundaries.","These vortices had opposite signs on the two sides of laminar zones and were sustained by baroclinic generation."]}

{"main_idea":"The text introduces a parametric toolbox to simulate single point incremental forming, with a focus on micro-SPIF. It says the method is checked against experiments and can predict defect-free micropart production.","key_points":["SPIF can make complex sheet parts without special tools, but it has thinning, defects, and long working time.","Scientists use formability tests, force curves, and forming limit diagrams to study the process.","Finite element simulation is useful, but accurate modeling depends on elements, algorithms, material models, contact, and toolpath strategy.","The paper develops a fully parametric toolbox for micro-SPIF and validates it with experimental data."]}

{"main_idea":"The text studies community-based tourism projects in Georgia and Armenia. It says the idea is often vague, but it can help protect culture, support local products, and strengthen rural communities.","key_points":["The study examined 15 CBT projects in Armenia and Georgia from 2012 to 2018 using interviews and document analysis.","Many actors use CBT loosely, and the term is not clearly defined in official documents or tourism policy.","People see CBT as useful for cultural and nature protection, local products, jobs, and community building.","Successful projects often depend on strong cooperation between local leaders and national authorities, with many projects led by international aid programs."]}

{"main_idea":"The text reviews progress toward a circular economy in water, energy, and food between 2010 and 2020. It says integrated and transformative approaches are needed to cut waste, improve efficiency, and support sustainable development goals.","key_points":["The study uses a global systematic literature review from 2010 to 2020.","It focuses on water and energy efficiency linked to food production in a circular economy.","It identifies successes, opportunities, challenges, and pathways from the literature.","It argues that transformative approaches can help reach SDG 12 and reduce environmental damage."]}

{"main_idea":"The text studies how higher education and technology entrepreneurship support regional innovation. It says universities can help create the skills and research that new technology firms need.","key_points":["The text links a new technological order to a knowledge-based economy and growing demand for smart technologies.","It uses Kalmyk State University as an example of a regional university that can support an innovation ecosystem.","It says the state must create conditions where entrepreneurship can demand skilled workers and research from universities.","It argues that weak technological entrepreneurship helps explain low innovation in the Russian economy, and many startups fail because of marketing, management, and capitalization problems."]}

{"main_idea":"The text reports an ERP study on how people process subject-verb agreement errors in speech. It finds that the P600 effect is mainly seen when the error occurs at the end of the utterance.","key_points":["Earlier ERP studies often found LAN and P600 effects for subject-verb agreement violations.","The study tested whether utterance position and violation type change auditory processing of these errors.","Australian English-speaking adults listened to sentences with omission or commission errors in medial or final position.","The P600 was significant only for utterance-final violations, while negativity did not differ by condition."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains a study on how memory of the 1883 tsunami faded on Sebesi Island. It also looks at how recent disasters and local knowledge shape community memory today.","key_points":["The study uses archival research, oral history, and a longue durée approach.","It compares Sebesi with Smong knowledge from Simeulue to understand collective memory.","The data came from visits to Sebesi in 2019, 2020, and 2021, plus other written sources.","Sebesi is a farming and fishing island in Lampung Bay with a mixed population and a history tied to Krakatau and the sea."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains Civil Engineering Preliminaries Protocol (CEPP) for conventional contracts. It says better descriptions of preliminary items can reduce disputes and improve price accuracy.","key_points":["Civil engineering preliminaries are hard to price because they are subjective and uncertain.","In Malaysian conventional contracts, engineers prepare the bills and contractors price them.","Contractors may ask for clarification during tender, but they cannot write their own preliminaries.","CEPP is meant to reduce vagueness, ambiguity, duplication, and price variation."]}

{"main_idea":"This text summarizes a study on how product packaging affects consumer buying decisions for FMCG items. It says packaging elements and media exposure matter, but background color is not significant.","key_points":["The study examines the impact of packaging elements on consumer purchase notion and buying behavior.","It focuses on FMCG items and uses data from Hyderabad city.","A questionnaire was used with 825 respondents and SPSS analysis.","TV, newspapers, magazines, and the internet were significant, while background color was not significant."]}

{"main_idea":"This text discusses how audit tenure, going concern audit opinions, and market performance are related. It finds that audit tenure helps predict going concern opinions, and those opinions hurt market performance.","key_points":["Audit opinion tells users whether financial statements are fairly presented and whether the company may keep operating.","Going concern opinions can give useful information to the market and may affect stock returns.","Longer audit tenure may improve audit quality because auditors understand the client better.","The study reports that audit tenure positively affects going concern opinions, and going concern opinions negatively affect market performance."]}

{"main_idea":"The text critiques optimistic ideas about green technology, especially solar power, from a Marxist view. It argues that Promethean faith in technology hides social and ecological limits and should be abandoned.","key_points":["Debates on renewable energy are polarized, and critics are often treated as defenders of fossil fuels.","The paper focuses on contradictions in Promethean arguments for solar power within the political left.","It notes concerns about low power density, low net energy, and environmental justice in renewable energy systems.","It argues that Marxist scholarship should reject depoliticized views of technology to address climate change and the Anthropocene."]}

{"main_idea":"The text studies how poverty affects aspirations and behavior. It says poor people share the same basic biases as others, but poverty makes those biases more harmful and can trap them in low goals and low effort.","key_points":["The framework treats aspirations failure as a behavioral problem, not only a lack of material resources.","Both rich and poor have biased aspiration setting, but the poor face greater downside risk.","Greater risk makes the poor more pessimistic and less likely to invest effort in goals.","Poverty also narrows whose life experiences the poor use when forming beliefs and aspirations."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how risks in green building development are classified. It says this classification helps identify risks that affect value creation and value engineering.","key_points":["The literature does not agree on one clear way to classify green building risks.","The text groups risks into functional, financial, operational, environmental, and management clusters.","The goal of the classification is to support risk identification in value creation for green buildings.","Functional risks matter because building use affects operating cost and occupant productivity."]}

{"main_idea":"The text studies how management affects librarians' motivation for professional development. It argues that recognition, support, and knowledge management may shape self-esteem and willingness to learn.","key_points":["The article focuses on professional development in academic libraries and how managers affect it.","It says librarians need ongoing learning because information work is changing fast.","It links management support and social recognition to motivation and self-esteem.","It uses a 2016 anonymous survey of Norwegian academic librarians to study these questions."]}

{"main_idea":"The text reviews smart port logistics in Ukraine under sustainable development. It says ports need better balance between economic, environmental, and social goals, and state regulation matters when competition is weak.","key_points":["The study uses Ukrainian, EU, and international sources, plus data from major ports and port organizations.","It applies several research methods to study smart ports, sustainable logistics, and port generations.","The discussion says many older models of sustainable development are too static and unbalanced.","It also explains that a port may need state regulation if competition is weak, while the English model fits strong competition."]}

{"main_idea":"The text reviews ways to measure income inequality in Russian households. It says both absolute and relative measures are needed, and it explains why the Gini index and newer corrections may still miss some gaps.","key_points":["Income inequality is the gap between poor and rich incomes.","Absolute and relative measures both matter for comparing inequality over time.","The Gini coefficient is common because it is simple and easy to read.","Bonferroni, median-based Gini, and Zenga aim to better capture inequality, especially for poor groups."]}

{"main_idea":"The text studies how bovine host miRNAs may affect bovine coronavirus infection. It suggests some miRNAs could help explain tissue tropism, immune control, and possible markers for infection, but they still need validation.","key_points":["BCoV infects both respiratory and enteric tracts in cattle, and the reason for this dual tropism is not well known.","The study used 18 BCoV genomes and bioinformatic tools to find host miRNAs that target the viral genome and host genes.","Four miRNAs may target the BCoV spike protein and may also affect immune suppression pathways.","Other miRNAs may affect IFN and RIG-I signaling and could serve as diagnostic or genetic markers, but more studies are needed."]}

{"main_idea":"The text studies telomere attrition in dairy cattle across life. It finds that telomere loss is linked to weather stress and shorter productive lifespan.","key_points":["RLTL was measured many times in 305 female dairy cattle across their lives.","Telomere shortening was more common than lengthening, especially in early life.","Hotter summers were linked to greater telomere attrition.","Average telomere attrition predicted shorter productive lifespan better than average TL or one early-life TL measure."]}

{"main_idea":"The text describes a mouse study of how corneal nerves heal after direct laser cuts. It finds that healing depends on the nerve pattern, and some cuts cause degeneration while others leave a fluorescent repair response.","key_points":["Thy1-YFP mice were used to image corneal nerves before and after in situ laser transection.","Three laser cut patterns were tested: point, segmental, and annular transection.","Corneal stromal nerves showed two main patterns, and these patterns were different even in the same eye or littermates.","Laser cuts caused different degeneration and regeneration outcomes, and loss of beta-3 tubulin staining confirmed nerve transection."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how to create adversarial examples for natural language. It says this is harder than in images, so the authors use a genetic algorithm that works in a black-box setting and keeps changes small, semantic, and grammatical.","key_points":["Image attack methods do not transfer well to language because word changes are visible and words are discrete tokens.","Simple embedding tricks can still make sentences unnatural and break syntax.","The attack assumes only black-box access, with queries and confidence scores, not model details.","The proposed method uses gradient-free genetic algorithms to make few word replacements while keeping meaning and coherence."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains what educational games are and how they can be used in chemistry teaching. It says games can help learning, but they work best with clear goals and teacher guidance.","key_points":["Educational games are games with a didactical purpose that support learning.","Active student participation can deepen understanding in chemistry and other subjects.","Teacher guidance before, during, and after play can improve motivation and learning.","Games can help students learn chemistry concepts, but some studies say they work only for certain content and clear objectives."]}

{"main_idea":"The text describes how GaAs/InAlAs(111)A quantum dots were grown and measured for single-photon emission. It shows that the dots are very low in density and can be studied one by one with optical spectroscopy.","key_points":["The samples were grown by solid-source MBE on InP(111)A substrates with GaAs quantum dots between InAlAs barriers.","The growth conditions were chosen to make a very low dot density of about 2 per square micrometer.","PL and micro-PL at 5 K were used to study the optical emission from the dot ensemble and single dots.","FSS and g(2)(τ) were measured with narrow filtering, a Fabry-Perot etalon, and a Hanbury Brown and Twiss setup."]}

{"main_idea":"The text describes a system for giving tourist information to travelers on public transport. It says the system must work with many device types and use local wireless networks, because normal central services and car-based services are too limited.","key_points":["Current traveler information services usually rely on a central server and advanced mobile devices.","These services have limited personalization and are mainly designed for private car drivers.","The proposed system gives tourist information during public transport trips through accessible local wireless networks.","It must support device heterogeneity, interoperability, scalability, and spontaneous interaction in vehicle environments."]}

{"main_idea":"The text lists machine-learning methods for blood glucose pattern classification and anomaly detection in type 1 diabetes. It shows that many models use CGM or other physiological data to detect hypoglycemia, hyperglycemia, or abnormal glucose patterns.","key_points":["The methods include support vector machines, neural networks, decision trees, Bayesian models, and fuzzy systems.","Many studies use CGM data together with signals such as heart rate, QTc, meals, or insulin infusion data.","The reported results are often measured by sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and related scores.","The main goal is early and reliable detection of dangerous glucose events and abnormal patterns."]}

{"main_idea":"This study compares two soccer teaching programmes for school-age students. It looks at Direct Instruction and Tactical Games Approach to see how similar they are and how their training load differs.","key_points":["The study designed two homogeneous didactic units with 29 tasks and 12 sessions each.","It compared Direct Instruction and Tactical Games Approach using SIATE variables and statistical tests.","The two programmes had the same main pedagogical features and game content.","They differed in external training load, which is important for judging their similarity."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains the methods used for a UK symposium on health inequalities research. It says how participants were chosen, how the focus groups were run, and how the discussion data were analyzed.","key_points":["The event was a 2-day symposium in Edinburgh in December 2012 with 87 participants from many sectors.","Participants were selected for their work in health inequalities research, policy, practice, or advocacy.","Fourteen focus groups were held, and people were grouped by profession and research method for the discussions.","The talks were recorded, anonymized, coded in NVivo 10, and analyzed using a thematic framework."]}

{"main_idea":"The text introduces a study on memorable duty-free shopping experiences for Chinese tourists. It says the study looks at shopping benefits and how they shape brand attitude, brand preference, and word-of-mouth.","key_points":["Korea has many duty-free shops, and they compete strongly for Chinese tourists.","Chinese tourists make a very large share of duty-free sales in Korea.","The study focuses on utilitarian and hedonic shopping benefits as causes of memorable experiences.","It also tests whether memorable experiences lead to brand attitude, brand preference, and word-of-mouth."]}

{"main_idea":"The text introduces risk in business and explains why it matters for management and bankruptcy prediction. It says firms need tools to measure risk and build models that can predict bankruptcy.","key_points":["Risk is a basic feature of firms because the future is uncertain.","Risk can bring extra benefits or threaten a business's survival.","Risk management treats risk as part of the effort to create firm value.","Altman was a pioneer in bankruptcy prediction with a five-variable discriminant model."]}

{"main_idea":"The text discusses sharia life insurance and how tabarru contracts and income relate to customer choices at AIA Sharia Unit. It says these factors can affect tabarru fund results and the company’s performance.","key_points":["Sharia insurance must follow Islamic law and avoid gharar, maysir, and riba.","Tabarru uses risk sharing and charitable contributions instead of risk transfer and premiums.","The tabarru fund depends on participant contributions, investment income, and claims.","AIA Sharia Unit shows falling contributions and fluctuating income and claims, with a large tabarru deficit in 2020."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how Social Security figures your retirement benefit. It also says when to claim can greatly change your payment, especially for couples and surviving spouses.","key_points":["Social Security uses your lifetime earnings, indexes them for inflation, and averages your 35 highest years.","Missing years are counted as zeros, so filling them can raise your benefit.","You can start benefits at 62, but waiting until full retirement age or later can increase the amount.","Spousal, ex-spousal, and survivor benefits have special rules, and each family should weigh health, work plans, income needs, and longevity."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how to get a Maryland commercial learner’s permit and commercial driver’s license. It says you must bring the right documents, pay the fee, and pass the required tests.","key_points":["You can get the commercial drivers manual from the MVA website or a full-service MVA office if you do not have internet access.","To get a learner’s permit or transfer an out-of-state license, you must show proof of identity, Social Security number, and Maryland residency.","A DOT card is required for all commercial vehicle drivers, and it must come from a health care provider after a physical exam.","You must pay the fee, complete the application and tests, then schedule and pass the skills test with a registered and insured commercial vehicle."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains how to find a property deed and read its legal description. It also warns that deed errors must be corrected the legal way before you rely on them.","key_points":["The deed is usually kept at the county recorder or assessor office where the land is located.","You may find a deed online, or you may need to request it in person and pay a fee.","The legal description may also appear on property tax statements, but you should verify it with the assessors office.","If a deed has an error, it must be re-executed and recorded again, and legal help is recommended."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains how to find and order a death certificate. It also explains who can access records and what to do when records are closed or the death happened outside the country.","key_points":["Start by finding the city and state where the death occurred, using relatives, online searches, or local obituaries.","Each state keeps its own vital records, and some deaths are filed in the county where they happened.","Closed-record states limit access to certain people, and others may only get an informational copy with private details removed.","You can order a death certificate online, by letter, or in person, and fees and office rules vary by state."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how to appeal a Social Security denial. It says the SSA appeal process has several levels and strict time rules.","key_points":["The SSA handles disability and retirement benefits, and a denial comes with a letter explaining the reason.","You must request an appeal within 60 days of the negative determination letter.","Disability claims can start online, but retirement denials require a written appeal form.","The appeals levels are reconsideration, hearing, Appeals Council review, and then possible federal court review."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how to get a marriage license in Florida. It also explains the papers, fees, waiting rules, and who can officiate the marriage.","key_points":["Call your local county courthouse to learn the county rules and make an appointment if needed.","Both people must go in person, and they must bring valid photo ID and any required original or certified records.","A Florida marriage license costs a set fee, and a counseling class may reduce the cost or remove some waiting rules.","The license must be used within the time limit, signed after the wedding, and later you can order certified copies for name changes and records."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains how to apply for a plumbing license in New Jersey. It says which application to use and what rules and fees you must meet before taking the exams.","key_points":["If you have not finished an apprenticeship or a related degree, you should apply for an apprenticeship.","If you have an apprenticeship but less than one year of approved work experience, you should apply as a journeyman.","If you have both apprenticeship and journeyman work, usually 5 years or more, you should apply for master plumber status.","Applicants must meet age, bond, education, work proof, background check, and form requirements, and they must pay the application and exam fees."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains how to report tips to ICE and how to find or ask about people in detention. It says online tips need contact information, while anonymous reports and detention help use different phone lines and tools.","key_points":["Online tips about crimes like human trafficking or immigrant exploitation must include your name, email address, and phone number.","If you want to stay anonymous, you must use ICE's toll-free tip line.","The tip lines for child exploitation or human trafficking are available 24 hours a day, seven days a week.","The detention reporting line and online detainee locator are for people asking about detainees, and the locator only searches adults over 18."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains how to change an Arizona driver license or ID address online. It says you must keep your address current, and a missed change can lead to a ticket.","key_points":["Arizona DOT handles driver licenses and identification cards.","You should keep your address current so you get renewal notices and other mail.","You may not use the online service during routine maintenance times.","You need personal details, your old and new addresses, and a new card costs a fee if requested."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains how county tax abatement works. It says abatement can forgive some taxes, but it is not an appeal about a wrong assessment and is only granted in some cases.","key_points":["Abatement may be available for family illness, probate, poverty, or a county listing mistake not tied to valuation.","The board does not have to grant abatement, and approval is discretionary and may vary by state.","You should file the request with the county office and include documents that support your reason.","The board gives a written decision, and you may be able to appeal a denial with legal help."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how Social Security retirement and disability benefits are paid. It also explains payment timing, electronic payment options, and when benefits may be taxed.","key_points":["Benefits are paid monthly by direct deposit into your bank account after they are due.","For retirement benefits, the payment day depends on your birth date or the birth date on which the claim is based.","Direct deposit is most common, but you can also use the Direct Express card or an electronic transfer account.","You may have to pay federal tax on benefits if your income is above the stated limits or if you file separately while married."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains how to apply by mail for an Ohio birth certificate copy. It says you must send the right form, ID, documents, and fee, and the process takes about three weeks.","key_points":["You can apply by mail if you are not in Ohio or cannot apply in person.","You need a completed application form and the right identification or legal documents.","The fee is $21.50 for each copy, and mail requests do not take cash or credit cards.","Send the materials to the Ohio Vital Statistics office or the local health department, and allow about three weeks."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how to get married in Washington. It gives the legal requirements, the application process, and the rules for the license and ceremony.","key_points":["Both partners must meet age and relationship rules, and minors need extra consent or court approval.","You do not have to live in Washington, and a license from any county can be used anywhere in the state.","You can apply in person, online, or by mail, and you must provide valid ID, SSN details or a declaration, and the fee.","After the license is issued, you must wait three days, marry within 60 days, use a proper officiant and two witnesses, and return the signed license within 30 days."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains who can enter Dubai without a visa and who can get a visa on arrival. It also gives the passport, ticket, and visa rules for these visitors.","key_points":["Citizens of GCC states do not need a visa to enter Dubai.","Citizens of 33 listed countries can get a visa on arrival if they meet basic requirements.","A passport valid for at least six months and a confirmed roundtrip ticket are required.","Germany and the United States also have longer-term visa options with different rules and fees."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains how to get a Delaware birth certificate in person. You must bring the right forms, ID, and payment, or your request may be delayed.","key_points":["You need a completed application for a certified copy of a Delaware birth certificate.","If you want your own birth certificate, you must show a copy of your official photo ID.","If you request someone else’s birth certificate, you usually need legal proof of your right to get it.","The fee is $25.00, and you must pay by personal check or money order, or use VitalChek for credit card payment."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how to register to vote and return mail ballots in Colorado, Oregon, and Washington. It also gives deadlines, required ID rules, and ballot return options for each state.","key_points":["All three states allow online voter registration, but Washington and Colorado need a state ID or driver’s license number.","Colorado, Oregon, and Washington each have different registration deadlines and websites.","If you do not have ID in Colorado or Washington, you can print the form and mail it or drop it off.","Voters can return ballots by mail, at official drop-off sites, or at the county board of elections, and Colorado also allows in-person voting with a mailed ballot."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains how employers enroll in E-Verify and use it to check whether workers are eligible to work in the U.S. It also says employers must review and sign the MOU and follow the system's rules.","key_points":["E-Verify is a DHS service that employers use to verify employee work eligibility in the U.S.","Employers should review the E-Verify video and quick reference guide before enrolling.","The enrollment process needs company and authorized user information and begins with four setup questions.","After enrollment, employers log in, open a case, enter I-9 data, and get the employment result."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains how to register to vote in Arizona and what to bring on Election Day. It says you must meet citizenship, residency, age, and felony-restoration rules, and you must show proof of identity when voting.","key_points":["You may register if you are a U.S. citizen, live in Arizona, and will be 18 by the next general election.","If you were convicted of a felony, you must wait until your rights have been restored before voting.","First-time registrants or people who moved to another county must complete the form and submit proof of citizenship if needed.","On Election Day, vote at the correct polling place and bring proof of identity, but you do not need the registration card."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains the rules for getting a Missouri marriage license. It says the license can be used statewide, but both people must apply in person and several age, ID, and marriage rules apply.","key_points":["County offices may have different fees, payment methods, and filing hours.","Both parties must be present, and a parent or guardian is needed for some applicants under 18.","A prior marriage must be ended at least 30 days before applying, and close relatives cannot marry.","The license is issued immediately, expires after 30 days if not used, and the officiant must return it within 15 days."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains who needs a PG or GROL license and how to get it. It says the license is for certain radio jobs and is valid for life after passing the required exams.","key_points":["The PG or GROL license is needed for jobs such as radio work on Great Lakes vessels and some aircraft roles.","Applicants must pass the licensing exam, be able to send and receive spoken English messages, and be a U.S. resident or legally eligible to work in the country.","Element 1 has 24 questions on basic radio law and operating practice, and you must get at least 18 correct.","Element 3 has 100 questions on general radiotelephone topics, and a radar endorsement needs Element 8 with 50 questions and 38 correct answers to pass."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains the mitral valve and mitral valve prolapse. It says MVP is often harmless, but backflow can sometimes cause symptoms or serious heart problems.","key_points":["The mitral valve helps blood flow one way through the left side of the heart.","Mitral valve prolapse happens when the valve flaps are floppy and do not close tightly.","Most people with MVP have no symptoms and need no treatment.","Regular dental care and follow-up can help lower the rare risk of infection and other problems."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains what blood thinners are and why people may need them. It also says they must be used carefully because they can cause bleeding and other side effects.","key_points":["Blood thinners prevent new blood clots and can stop existing clots from getting bigger.","They may be needed for heart or blood vessel disease, atrial fibrillation, valve replacement, surgery risk, or congenital heart defects.","The main types are anticoagulants and antiplatelets, and antiplatelets are mainly used after a heart attack or stroke.","People should follow directions, watch for interactions, get blood tests if needed, and call a provider for signs of serious bleeding."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains refractive errors and how they affect vision. It says they happen when the eye does not focus light correctly on the retina, causing blurry vision and often needing correction.","key_points":["Refractive errors can be caused by an eye that is too long or too short, a changed cornea, or a lens that is less flexible with age.","Common types are nearsightedness, farsightedness, astigmatism, and presbyopia.","Anyone can have refractive errors, and they are very common, but family history and age can raise the chance.","They are diagnosed with a comprehensive eye exam and are usually treated with glasses, contact lenses, or sometimes laser eye surgery."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains what angioplasty is and how it is used to treat blocked coronary arteries. It also says the procedure can improve blood flow, but it does not cure coronary artery disease.","key_points":["Angioplasty widens narrow or blocked coronary arteries to improve blood flow to the heart.","Doctors use it to reduce angina and to limit heart damage during or right after a heart attack.","The procedure is usually done in a hospital cath lab through a blood vessel in the arm, wrist, or groin.","Possible risks include bruising, soreness, bleeding, serious bleeding, blood clots, and the artery narrowing again."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains respiratory syncytial virus, or RSV, and how it spreads, causes illness, and can be prevented. It also says RSV can be mild, but it can cause severe disease in infants, older adults, and other high-risk people.","key_points":["RSV is a common respiratory virus that usually causes cold-like symptoms but can lead to serious lung infections.","It spreads through coughs, sneezes, close contact, and touching contaminated surfaces.","Symptoms often begin 4 to 6 days after infection and can include runny nose, cough, fever, wheezing, and trouble breathing in young infants.","There is no specific treatment, so care is supportive, and prevention includes vaccines, medicines for some babies and children, and hygiene steps."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains what suicide is and why it is a serious public health problem. It also gives warning signs, risk factors, and steps for getting help right away.","key_points":["Suicide means taking one's own life, and a suicide attempt is self-harm that does not end in death.","Suicide can affect anyone, but risk can be higher with past attempts, mental health or substance use disorders, family history, violence, guns at home, prison, exposure to suicide, illness, stress, or certain ages.","Warning signs include talking about death, making a plan, buying weapons or pills, hopelessness, heavy substance use, agitation, isolation, mood swings, and saying goodbye.","If there are warning signs, get help right away, call 911 in an emergency, ask about suicide, keep the person safe, stay with them, and connect them to 988 or the Veterans Crisis Line."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains what healthy living means and why it matters. It says small daily changes can improve health and lower the risk of serious disease.","key_points":["Healthy living means caring for your body and mind with good daily choices.","Some health factors cannot be changed, but many habits can be improved.","Small, steady changes are easier to keep and can become routine.","Healthy living includes healthy food, exercise, sleep, stress care, and regular checkups."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains what infectious diseases are and how germs can cause them. It also says they can often be prevented, but some infections may only be treated by easing symptoms.","key_points":["Infectious diseases are caused by germs such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites.","People can get these diseases through direct contact, indirect contact, bites, or contaminated food, water, soil, or plants.","Symptoms can be mild or severe, and some infections can be life-threatening.","Some infections can be treated with medicines, and prevention includes vaccination, handwashing, food safety, condoms, and not sharing personal items."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains diabetes and focuses on type 2 diabetes. It says type 2 diabetes can often be prevented or delayed with healthy lifestyle changes.","key_points":["Diabetes is a disease that makes blood glucose too high.","Type 2 diabetes happens when the body does not make enough insulin or does not use it well.","Many factors can raise the risk, including age, weight, family history, race, and certain health conditions.","Prevention or delay may include losing weight, eating well, exercising, not smoking, and sometimes using medicine."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains what obesity is, how it is diagnosed, and how it is treated. It also shows that obesity raises the risk of many health problems, but weight loss can help lower that risk.","key_points":["Obesity means having too much body fat, and an adult BMI of 30 or more is considered obesity.","Obesity can develop over time when calorie intake is higher than calorie use, and many factors can affect weight.","Doctors may diagnose obesity using health history, a physical exam, BMI, waist size, and sometimes blood or imaging tests.","Treatment may include diet and exercise changes, counseling, medicines, or surgery for severe cases."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains glaucoma, a group of eye diseases that can damage the optic nerve and cause vision loss. It also says early exams and treatment can help slow the disease, but untreated glaucoma can lead to blindness.","key_points":["Glaucoma can affect one or both eyes and may have no early symptoms.","The most common type is open-angle glaucoma, and angle-closure glaucoma can cause sudden eye pain and blurred vision.","A comprehensive eye exam can diagnose glaucoma with dilated eye checks, visual field testing, and tonometry.","There is no cure or prevention, but eye drops and other treatments can lower eye pressure and protect vision."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains what mammograms are and why people get them. It says mammograms can find breast cancer early, but they also have limits and risks.","key_points":["A mammogram is an x-ray picture of the breast used to look for early breast cancer.","Screening mammograms are for people with no signs of breast cancer and may lower deaths in women ages 40 to 74.","Screening mammograms can also miss cancer, cause false alarms, and expose people to radiation.","Diagnostic mammograms are for people with symptoms or special breast concerns, and an abnormal result does not always mean cancer."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains what a caregiver is and how caregiving can affect the caregiver. It says caregiver stress can harm health, so caregivers should seek support and care for themselves.","key_points":["A caregiver helps someone who needs support with daily life, health care, or decisions.","Caregivers can be family, friends, or paid professionals, and they may care at home, in a hospital, or from a distance.","Caregiving can be rewarding, but it can also be stressful and overwhelming.","Caregiver stress can lead to physical and mental health problems, and support, rest, and self-care can help reduce it."]}

{"main_idea":"The text explains what an inactive lifestyle is and why it is harmful. It also gives simple ways to start moving more at home and at work.","key_points":["An inactive lifestyle means a lot of sitting and very little or no exercise.","It can lead to weight gain, weaker muscles and bones, and other body changes.","It raises the risk of many long-term diseases and may increase early death.","People can start slowly and add more activity in daily life, at home, and at work."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains what kidneys do and what chronic kidney disease is. It says CKD damages the kidneys slowly and may lead to kidney failure.","key_points":["Kidneys filter blood, remove waste and extra water, and help balance body chemicals.","Chronic kidney disease means the kidneys are damaged and cannot filter blood well.","Diabetes and high blood pressure are the most common causes, and many people have no symptoms early on.","Treatment cannot cure CKD, but it may slow it, and healthy habits may help protect the kidneys longer."]}

{"main_idea":"This text explains cervical cancer screening and why it matters.
